2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
3.
The case of prosecution is that on the complaint of respondent No.2 filed on 05.04.2023, the police registered FIR.
It is alleged that the complainant married petitioner-accused No.1 in the year 2020.
She was residing in the matrimonial house at Chalkapur.
A child by name Pavana, aged one year, was born to them.
For the last six months, the accused persons conspiring for the second marriage of her husband and they used to physically and mentally harassing her.
On that back ground, on 03.04.2023 at 10.30 a.m., her father-in-law and mother-in-law said to be called their children for partitioning the ancestral property.
For that, accused No.2 told that there is loan of Rs.30 lakhs payable by him and there shall NC: 2024:KHC-K:5881 be six shares in the property.
There was no conscientious decision was taken in the house during talk.

In the mean while, at about 1.00 p.m., accused Nos.5 and 6 came from Kalaburagi and when they entered into the house,
accused No.5 started abusing the complainant in filthy language and asking the family members to send her out.
They said to be held her heir and assaulted with hands.
Her husband also joined and assaulted the complainant.
All the other accused joined and abetted, and quarreled with her and they thrown out her from the house.
4. Accused No.6 said to be trying to pelt stone on her and some how she escaped and she left near Hanuman temple.
Later, the people of the village informed her father.
Accordingly, at 4.00 p.m., her father came to her and took her to Katakachincholi hospital and thereafter, to Bidar hospital and later, filed the complaint.
Accordingly, the police investigated the matter and filed charge sheet.
Therefore, the petitioner- accused Nos.4 to 6 have filed this petition challenging the charge sheet filed against them.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the petitioners have been falsely implicated by the respondent No.2-complainant.
Accused No.4 is residing in some other place in Bidar District, whereas accused Nos.5 and 6 are residing at Kalaburagi.
There is no occasion for them for coming to complainant place and harass her or demand any dowry.

On the date of incident,
they went only to participate in the partition talk and they did not do anything, but respondent No.2 willfully filed the false complaint against them.
Therefore, conducting the criminal proceedings against the petitioners- accused is abuse of process of law.
It is further contended that the injury certificate produced would show that there is no injury sustained by the complainant.
Such being the case, the complaint is a false complaint.

Therefore, prays for allowing the petition.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 has seriously objected the petition and contended that accused No.4, who was already stayed in the house, came for partition talk and there was quarrel between them.
Accused Nos.5 and 6 went to Chalkapura, where the real problem started.

Accused Nos.5 and 6 assaulted the complainant with their NC: 2024:KHC-K:5881 hands,
pulling her hair and kicked her and thrown out the complainant from the house.

sentences.text: It is inhuman act done by the accused persons.
There is prima facie material placed for framing charge and for taking cognizance against the petitioners and for filing charge sheet.
Hence, prays for dismissing the petition.
7. The learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State supported the arguments made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
It is submitted that there is prima facie material in the case and there are eye witnesses to the incident.
Hence, prays for dismissing the petition.
8. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the records.
9. Admittedly, the marriage between accused No.1 and the complainant is not in dispute.
They are having a child aged about one year.
It is alleged that the accused persons were trying to got for second marriage of her husband by sending her out of the house.
On that back ground, all the accused assembled in the matrimonial house of the complainant on NC: 2024:KHC-K:5881 03.04.2023 11.30 p.m..
There was talk in respect of the property which was not settled.
Some other persons by name Shivaraj and Sanjeevkumar also came for settling the matter.
Later, they went out as accused Nos.5 and 6 came to the house at 1 p.m. where the quarrel took place.
They said to be assaulted the complainant with hands by holding her hair and abused her in filthy language.

There is specific allegation made by the complainant against accused Nos.5 and 6 that they came from Kalaburagi for partition talk and assembled for settling the dispute, but during quarrel, they assaulted her and she was thrown out of her house.

The statement of father of the complainant corroborates the statement of the complainant where he received information at 2.30 p.m. and then he went to Chalkapura and took his daughter who was standing near the temple and taken her to the hospital and after treatment, the complaint was filed.

10. Apart from that, one Kishore, Balabhim, Rachappa, Shivaraj and Voojinath, who are the villagers of the accused, have given evidence in support of the complainant, which reveals that it is possible and the presence of the petitioners at NC: 2024:KHC-K:5881 the time of the incident on 03.04.2023 at 1.00 p.m. in the matrimonial house of the complainant, cannot be doubted.
If at all any defence available, they can take the same at the time of cross examination and that itself not a ground to quash the proceedings.
In my view, it is a case triable by framing the charges against the accused persons.
11. Accordingly, the petition is devoid of merit and it is dismissed.
